question: When does Fluff of Fleetness gain and reset on-field ATK stacks, including switching and delayed packets?
decision: Start at zero stacks at combat start for an initially active wearer and on every real field entry. Every full world-time interval adds one self base-ATK percentage stack, up to five. Successful departure removes all stacks and invalidates its old timer; same-actor swaps and rejected switches do not reset. Admission precedes equal-time ticks, and ticks precede hits. Delayed hits sample current stacks at delivery. Permanent stacks are exported through the shared BuffManager and stop generating timers at cap. These clock/order/snapshot choices are tested model hypotheses.
availability: Frozen Global release availability remains unverified.
stop_condition: Check source curves/units, exact tick boundaries, cap, initial off-field ownership, no-op and failed switch, exit/reentry stale timers, delayed delivery, passive-only horizon snapshots, event limits and CLI/WASM/Worker parity.
return_condition: New initialization, world/real clock, stacking, snapshot, switching or release evidence conflicts with the model.
checks: 169 content and 124 core tests pass. T1-T5 bind .05/.06/.07/.08/.09 per stack and one-second intervals; native unit changes fail. Legal Mint native build receives two R5 stacks at two seconds, checked as (total ATK + base ATK * .18)/total ATK.

Independent event/damage oracle: 1000 base/total ATK * .5 DEF yields 500 before one second, 525 at one second, 600 just before five seconds and 625 at/after cap. Eight integration cases cover passive-only short/full horizons, exact boundaries, initial off-field entry, earned-stack removal, reentry/stale timers, no-op/failed switch, delayed delivery and event-limit snapshots. Generic core owner removal retains other sources/owners/effect IDs.

Public Mint/Fleetness T1-T5 with an Iroi teammate runs two continuing field cycles. With the existing two 250ms script swaps, Mint reenters at 7.05 seconds; hit times 0/1/5/7.3/9.1 seconds use 0/1/5/0/2 stacks. Independent ATK multipliers and permanent five-stack final snapshots agree. Full CLI/WASM report parity passes for all five scripts; the real Worker T5 run agrees with direct WASM.

TypeScript/production build, native_build and scenario_script tests pass. Changed Rust formatting passes. Core/content clippy passes allowing only the two pre-existing content metadata lints collapsible_if and single_element_loop. Native parity uses NTESIM_VERIFY_NATIVE=1 NTESIM_VERIFY_WEAPON=motor_candy; other weapons retain WASM/Worker checks.
Native animation timing, world/real pause interaction and release availability remain unresolved model limits. Frozen source bytes are unchanged.
